import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Fractional parts of sums of reciprocals of Catalan numbers $C(n)$

Catalan numbers $C(n) = \frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}$.

The sum $\sum_{i=j}^k \frac{1}{a(i)}$ of reciprocals of Catalan numbers.

*References:*
- [A000108](https://oeis.org/A000108)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA108


open Nat Real Finset

/--
Catalan numbers $C(n) = \frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}$.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.choose (2 * n) n) / (n + 1)

def aRat (n : ℕ) : ℚ := (a n : ℚ)⁻¹

/-- The sum $\sum_{i=j}^k \frac{1}{a(i)}$ of reciprocals of Catalan numbers. -/
def catalanReciprocalSum (j k : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  (Finset.Icc j k).sum aRat

/-- The index condition on $(j, k)$ from the conjecture: $0 < \min\{2,k\} \le j \le k$.
Since j and k are natural numbers, $0 < \min\{2,k\}$ is equivalent to $1 \le k$. -/
def IndexCond (j k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  1 ≤ k ∧ min 2 k ≤ j ∧ j ≤ k

open Int (fract)

/-- The fractional part of a rational number. -/
def fracPart (q : ℚ) : ℚ := fract q


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 5 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 14 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: All the rational numbers $\sum_{i=j}^k \frac{1}{a(i)}$ with
$0 < \min\{2,k\} \le j \le k$ have pairwise distinct fractional parts.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/108.wip.lean#L255"]
theorem catalanReciprocalSum_fracPart_inj : ∀ ⦃j₁ k₁ j₂ k₂ : ℕ⦄,
    IndexCond j₁ k₁ → IndexCond j₂ k₂ →
    (j₁, k₁) ≠ (j₂, k₂) →
    fracPart (catalanReciprocalSum j₁ k₁) ≠ fracPart (catalanReciprocalSum j₂ k₂) := by
    sorry

end OeisA108

reformulations.difference: The file keeps fractional parts in ℚ, whereas the cited formal proof computes them in ℝ after casting the rational sums.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Rat.cast_fract identifies the real cast of a rational fractional part with the fractional part of its real cast. Since ℚ → ℝ is injective, equality and inequality of fractional parts are preserved and reflected. The sums and index restrictions otherwise agree. The full quantified equivalence was proved in scratch.lean, and a separate kernel-checked bridge derives the current statement from the replayed linked proof.

review.notes: All five definitions, five test lemmas, and the main theorem were checked; no mathematical defects were found. Direct OEIS requests were blocked, so its maintained data mirror was used. The source states exactly the displayed index restriction and explicitly records the conjecture as proved, agreeing with research solved. Lean checks established that a is the standard Catalan sequence, natural-number division is exact, and every reciprocal has a positive denominator. IndexCond is equivalent both to the source inequalities and to (j,k)=(1,1) or 2≤j≤k; thus empty sums are excluded. Initial values match OEIS, and exact evaluation found distinct fractional parts for all 436 admissible intervals with k≤30. The linked proof was replayed in /workspace/review/linked108-check.lean after import/API compatibility edits and rephrasing one elementary helper proof. Both the replayed theorem and its bridge to the reviewed statement depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The reviewed file was not modified.
